concerns.text: T002 is tagged [P] and the Dependencies section claims 'T001 and T002 are parallelizable since they touch different files', but T002's own description says 'Generate data/derived/nlcd_{60,120,240,480}m_co.tif from the 30 m source' — a hard data dependency on T001's output data/raw/nlcd_30m_co.tif. Touching different code files does not make tasks parallel-safe; this is a consumer-before-producer risk if executed concurrently. Remove the [P] tag or restructure T002 to be testable on a fixture raster.

T011 is tagged [P] but its description requires citing 'the runtime/memory figures' produced by T010's data/results/runtime_report.json, and the Dependencies section itself concedes 'listed last so it can cite runtime figures'. A task that must read another task's output artifact is not parallel-safe; drop the [P] tag.

T005 (lambda calibration) reads 'the 30 m forest binary' produced by T003, but the stated execution order 'T001 → T002 → T003 → (T004, T005)' is correct only if T003 strictly precedes T005; the parenthetical grouping of T004/T005 is fine, but the Dependencies section should state the T003→T005 edge explicitly since T005's input is a T003 artifact, not a T002 artifact.
